Vilshynky Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews are believed to have arrived in Vilshynky in the late 18th century, reaching a peak of about 38 people by 1880 before declining steadily to just 13 or 14 by the interwar period. Hungarian forces arrived in March 1939; by 1941, only 6 Jews remained in the village. That year, families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi in Nazi-occupied Ukraine and murdered, and the remaining Jews of Vilshynky were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
